v%1$s · all data stays on this phone

It moves your phone contacts into an encrypted local vault: every record is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before it hits the disk, so the database holds no readable names or numbers. Paired with the caller ID overlay, even an unknown number shows you who it is.
Copy your system contacts in all at once; export them back any time after clearing the system, so uninstalling is never a risk
The key is generated by the system Keystore, never written to disk and never exportable — even if the database is copied away, its contents stay unreadable
Message content is encrypted as a whole, and you can read it, export it to CSV, or clear the originals in the system
Call history is kept encrypted, so numbers and durations never land in plain text — always available to search and export
Shows the caller\'s name in an overlay on incoming calls — identification only, no blocking, no recording, no uploading
No account, no server, no analytics — all data lives on this phone only

Every permission is required by the feature it belongs to, and each one is requested only when you open that feature — nothing is demanded all at once at startup:

· Contacts (read) — import your system contacts into the encrypted vault
· Contacts (write) — only needed to write the vault back to the system or clear the system contacts
· SMS (read) — import your system messages into the encrypted vault
· SMS (write) — the system only lets the default SMS app delete messages, so if it is not set, clearing takes you straight to the system settings page
· Call log (read) — import your system call history into the encrypted vault
· Phone state — dismiss the caller ID overlay after the call ends
· Overlay / notifications — show the caller ID card and the ongoing notification

There is no network permission, and no location, camera, microphone, or storage permission.
MIT licensed — feel free to build, modify, and redistribute it. The source contains no backend at all; every feature runs on your phone.

· Duplicate contacts are tagged as "Duplicate" automatically, so you can locate them by searching the number
· Uninstalling also wipes the encryption key — export to system contacts or export a CSV first
· SMS and call history need their own permissions, and are stored encrypted on this device only
· The caller ID overlay needs the "display over other apps" permission; some Chinese ROMs also require allowing pop-ups in the background
